# Step 2.226: names on the scoring screens

## Builder 1 (the rule in core and the reads)

What exists:

- R-33 as one function, `scoringNames` (`packages/core/src/modules/games/scoring-names.ts`), built on `showName`; on, the setting asks `showName` under full names with children confirmed, so a person's own request always holds. `namedRoster` applies it to a game's roster; places ("Player 1") per team, in roster order, for one the number and name do not tell apart.
- The setting `privacy.scorekeepersSeeFullNames` (declarations, `league.settings`, off; a value that cannot be read is off), read by `readScoringNameView` / `scoringNameSettingsOf`. Its messages are in `admin-settings.ts`. The generic settings page draws every declared setting, so it already shows under Privacy: builder 2 checks its wording and place after 2.227 lands.
- `GamesStore.listRoster(gameId, names)`: the database query (`list-game-roster.ts`, reads `visibility` and the child test in SQL), the stand-in world and core's memory store all name players by the rule, so every caller (tracker rosters, box score sheet, tracked grid, the worn-number reply) gets only the rule's names.
- Contract `TrackerRosterPlayer.ordinal` (T-478); the device keeps it (optional on `DevicePlayer`); `playerLabel` words "Player 1" and "Sam L. (player 2)".
- Decisions: R-33 (the lead's), T-478, T-479, T-480 in `decisions-pending/`; T4 §7 has the rule.
- Old games: names are read at view time, never saved with lines, so an old game's box score sheet reads by the rule too.

Run and passed: core games, standings, leagues; tracker and games-area features; contracts; the database tracker tests (youth: the served rosters hold "Player30 H." and nowhere "Heronfamily"; hidden league: no name until the setting is on); role matrix; the whole `apps/web/src/server`. Each new test was broken once by hand and failed.

For builder 2:

- The score page and the box score sheet (`box-score-page.tsx`, `tracked-grid-page.tsx`): they already get the rule's names; word `ordinal` there ("Player 1") from messages, and check the tiles (`scoring-view.ts` `shortName`) for a player with neither number nor name.
- The device dropping a game's stored roster once the game is ended and saved or another account signs in, never while live or taps wait (2.107 audit, M4).
- A database case with a removed child and an adult with initials, searched in the rosters answer, the stored copy and the box score sheet as served (here only in core's memory test); the settings switch; the browser proof at 390 wide; Admin → Teams with "Show as".

What I distrust:

- A page opened before this step parses the rosters address's answer strictly: `ordinal` is a new key, so its refresh fails until the page reloads, and its stored copy keeps the names it was sent before.
- `readScoringNameView` hands `readNamePolicy` rows with version 0 (it reads values only).
- The isolation case for `listGameRoster` runs with the setting on; no role-matrix row was added, as no command or read was added (the setting has its row through `settingRows(declaredSettings)`).

## Builder 4 (the fix round: one High, three Mediums)

What exists:

- T-487 (High): a fresh answer wins for names. `freshOverKept` (`device-rosters.ts`) lays the kept copy over a fresh answer only for a table-added player whose add still waits; the controller uses it when the device starts from its copy after a fetch answered, and fetches the rosters once opening is answered if none has. The real cause found: `markingOnAnswer` (`open-tracker-game.ts`) dropped `loadRosters`, so the tracker never fetched rosters fresh; it passes it through. The worker replaces its kept page with the page fetched fresh for the same account, after keeping every code file that page names (`pageCodeOf`; a file it cannot fetch leaves the old page).
- T-488: `forgetGame` also asks the worker (`forgetTrackerPageOfGame`) to drop that game's kept page; the worker checks the queue itself (`mayForgetGamePage`). `letGoOfGame` is cleared when the status leaves final (the Low, two lines).
- Tiles: `tracker.player.namePlace` is "Player {place} · {name}".
- R-33's pending file, T-483's and T4 §7 now say what is true: People, Teams and the bin show the recorded name, the person's page the request, "Show as" in the lists with step 2.146.
- `scoring-names-test` (39 checks): the restored check (off again, a reload: within 15 s neither storage nor kept page holds "Hawkins"/"Bearsley"); three same-named table players read "Player 1 ·", "Player 2 ·", "Player 3 ·" before the ellipsis at 390 wide; surnames searched with `i`; the 15 s wait now waits for the game and "R. Q." to be stored.

Breaks seen failing: the kept copy always laid (2 controller tests), no unknown player laid (1), the worker not replacing (1), code not required first (1), the queue ignored (1), the page not dropped (1), `forgetPage` not called or taps ignored (1 each), `loadRosters` dropped (1 unit test; the browser check failed on it before the mend, "srleagues-tracker-games/games (rosters)").

Run and passed: the tracker feature (61 files, 838); `npm run check`; `npm run typecheck`; `packages/site/src/messages` with `tracker-rosters-reply.test.ts`; `scoring-names-test`. See the report for what was not run.

Left / polish:

- T-484's exception: while taps of a game wait, a copy stored before the step shows names as recorded until they are saved.
- The scorer's activity was not searched for names.
- The tiles' check was not run against the old wording (it was written with the new one).
- Four `open-tracker-game.test.ts` checks now expect the server's rosters (the fetch on opening); the T-484 one writes the old copy back to keep its case.

Pending decisions of the lane: R-33 (Decided for you), T-478, T-479, T-480, T-483, T-484, T-487, T-488 (Agreed, delegated).

## Builder 5 (the second fix round: the open game, the Undo failures)

What exists:

- `scoring-plays-test`: the four "one tap on Undo took the basket back" failures were the stale name too. The score after the Undo was right (home 4, away 3 is the expected value); the same check also asked for the label "Undo #9 Pia Hawkins +2", and R-33 gives "Undo #9 Pia H. +2" (Pia is the seeded child). Undo was not broken. The four names corrected; the check's detail now prints the labels beside the score.
- T-489, an open game asks again: the controller fetches the rosters when the page is shown again and when the network is back (both already did, through `backOnline`), and every five minutes (`rostersAgainMs`), carried on the session's renewal (every 5 s while held), no timer of its own. A fresh answer that changed what is stored, and the network back, call `renewKeptPage`; the page posts `trackerWorkerRenewGameMessage` (`renewTrackerPageOfGame`), and the worker fetches the page fresh and replaces its kept one only for the same account (`mayRenewKeptPage`, code kept first); it never keeps a page it had not kept. Not after the game was let go of (T-488).
- Unit tests: the three moments each fetch; a fetch with no answer changes neither the rosters shown or stored nor the kept page; a waiting tap keeps its place and state and is sent once, in order; the kept page is replaced when names changed and at the network back, not when nothing changed; the worker replaces for the same account (a tap waiting), keeps it for a failed fetch or another account, keeps none it had not.
- `scoring-names-test` (50 checks): switched off with the game left open, no reload (a mark on the page proves it), the five minutes forced on the page's own clock (Playwright's `clock`, as `bad-wifi-test` does, so no setting of the product was added): the tiles, the stored rosters and the kept page hold no full name. With no signal #41 added at the table and tapped three times; the signal back and fresh rosters in, #41 is still on the screen, the score up exactly 3 and the box score sheet's points box for #41 is 3.

Breaks seen failing: no five-minute fetch (2 unit tests; the browser check: "stored rosters" and "kept page" still held the names); no kept-page renewal on a change (1); a failed fetch renewing (2); the page shown again not fetching (2); the worker not replacing (1); the worker ignoring the account (1); the fresh answer losing #41 (the browser check: "#41 is still on the screen").

Run and passed (each its own command, the top read): `scoring-names-test` (50), `scoring-screen-test` (1002), `scoring-plays-test` (709), `tracker-offline-test`, `tracker-route-test` (79), `players-panel-test`, `live-game-test` (48), `draft-scorer-taps-test` (15); `npm run check`; `npm run typecheck`; the tracker feature (844); the whole `apps/web/src/server` (91 files, 1202); `npm run format:check`; `node --test tests/pending-decisions.test.mjs` (11). No message was added.

Left:

- Item 3's second half: a final game with one tap set aside keeping its kept page until the tap is saved (T-488) was not tried in a browser (setting a tap aside needs a refusal the stand-in does not give easily); the worker's rule has its unit tests.
- The waiting-tap unit test was not broken by hand on its own.

What I distrust:

- A read-only page (another device holds the game) does not renew, so it asks only when shown again or back online (said in T-489).
- The kept page's renewal is one extra page fetch at each network back and each changed answer.
